newsitem.title: FRANCE: Dassault, Aerospatiale merger seen by spring.
newsitem.headline: Dassault, Aerospatiale merger seen by spring.

text.p: France's government-owned Aerospatiale and combat plane maker Dassault Aviation will merge this spring, with privatisation of the new company to follow promptly, a defence ministry official said Wednesday.
"If we put everything together ... at the end of the spring, the merger will be entirely complete," the offical said.
"As for the privatisation of the new group, the government wants it to be done in the immediate aftermath and will ask the two company chairmen to think about it now and make proposals."
The finance ministry said Tuesday that Aerospatiale and Dassault would be merged to form a company with a single supervisory board and one set of executive directors.
It called the merger the first stage of the privatisation of the new group but did not give a timetable for the process.
The government said it would ask France's independent privatisation commission to fix the two companies' values and give its opinion on the merger terms.
Once the commission has given its views, the government will formally approve the final transaction terms, which will be carried out with approval of stock market authorities.

The government's decision to wait for commission approval before setting final terms of its plans is a sign the government is treading carefully in the Aerospatiale/Dassault matter and a recognition that it cannot afford another misstep after its bungling of the sale of Thomson SA last year.

The government abandoned its plan to sell Thomson to conglomerate Lagardere after the privatisation commission objected to the sale of the Thomson Multimedia unit to South Korean firm Daewoo Electronics.
The decision to freeze the sell-off, seen as inept at best and racist at worst, sparked an official protest from the South Korean government and scorn in financial and political circles.
